capabilities.target: user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Recalled memories, which can originate from untrusted web content saved via memory.save, are explicitly granted the authority of the user's own instructions with no verification step.
The agent is told to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions with no filtering criteria, scope limit, or sensitivity check.

controls.name: Provenance tagging and trust-level enforcement on memory writes
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the memory store itself (tagging writes with source and trust_level and refusing to surface untrusted-provenance entries as instructions), so it does not depend on model compliance.

controls.name: Orchestration-layer segregation of recalled memory from instruction-bearing context
controls.decay_rationale: If the orchestration layer places recalled memory in a non-authoritative data block that tool-invocation logic cannot parse as directives, the model's willingness to 'obey' the content becomes irrelevant.

controls.name: Least-privilege scoping of drive.read away from confidential files by default
controls.decay_rationale: A credential that cannot read confidential files cannot be made to leak them regardless of what the model is instructed to do.

controls.name: Human approval gate on mail.send with raw-action review
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action approval gate is enforced outside the model and does not decay with capability, though it can still suffer approval fatigue at high volume.

controls.name: Recipient allowlist / confirmation bound to system-of-record contacts for mail.send
controls.decay_rationale: Binding the destination to the system of record rather than to model output does not decay with capability.

findings.title: Memory poisoning via untrusted web content later treated as trusted instructions, enabling drive exfiltration (TC5 memory laundering)

attack_path.note: Untrusted web content fetched during research
Agent is instructed to save 'anything useful' from research into memory
No provenance tagging; entries are never reviewed by the user
Recalled at next session start, injected into the system prompt, explicitly treated as the user's own instructions
Poisoned 'instruction' can direct the agent to read the user's full confidential drive
Poisoned 'instruction' can direct the agent to email the content externally

forecast.watch_signal: New research connectors or tools that feed additional untrusted sources into memory.save, or model upgrades that make injected 'memory instructions' more convincing and harder to distinguish from genuine user preferences.

evidence.observation: The prompt instructs the agent to save 'anything useful' from research (sourced from untrusted web content) into memory, and to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of every session, with no provenance check.
memory.save accepts free text with no provenance tagging, and the user never reviews saved memory entries before they are recalled and re-injected into the system prompt.

recommendations.action: Tag memory entries with provenance (source, trust_level) at write time, enforced by the memory store, and refuse to treat untrusted-provenance entries as instructions.
Segregate recalled memory into a clearly non-authoritative, data-only context rather than the instruction-bearing system prompt, enforced by the orchestration layer rather than by prompt wording.
Log all memory writes and periodically audit for imperative or instruction-like content originating from fetched web pages.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: memory treated as instructions drives full-drive read and unrestricted email send (TC1)

attack_path.note: Memory recalled and treated as the user's own instructions, per prompt.md:4
Instruction directs the agent to read the user's full, confidential drive
Instruction directs the agent to send the content to an arbitrary external address with no approval

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Any widening of drive_read scope, any autonomy change allowing longer unattended runs, or model upgrades making injected instructions more convincing - none of these are currently gated by any control, so the path is already fully open.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval, and drive.read covers the user's full drive including confidential work files; recalled memories (traceable to untrusted web content) are injected as instructions that can direct both tools in sequence.
The prompt explicitly instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions, removing any barrier between injected content and tool-directing authority.

recommendations.action: Require human approval with raw-action review (full recipient and body visible, not a model summary) before mail.send executes, especially when the draft was influenced by recalled memory or web content.
Scope drive.read credentials away from confidential/restricted files by default, or require step-up approval to read confidential documents in a session that will also send email.
Add a recipient allowlist / confirmation for mail.send bound to a system-of-record contact list, excluding attacker-writable or arbitrary external recipients.

rating.rationale: Both findings reach critical risk with no mitigating controls in place. Untrusted web content can be persisted into cross-session memory with no provenance, the prompt directs the agent to treat recalled memory as the user's own instructions, and the resulting 'instructions' can freely read the user's entire confidential drive and send email to any external address with no approval, egress restriction, or credential scoping. No declared or verified control sits on either the memory-poisoning path or the drive-read-then-send path, so residual equals inherent at the rubric floor with zero credits. No modeled trigger can push the tier higher than critical, so forecast equals residual. Autonomy is scored A3 with no attended-step or runtime bound and a self-modifying memory channel injected directly into the system prompt, so the inherent autonomy modifier also applies.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided; capability scope for memory.save, mail.send, and drive.read is inferred from the runtime notes and prompt text, so confidence rests on declared design rather than verified configuration.

The A3 autonomy level and the can_modify_own_config classification are inferred from the described memory-injection behavior (recalled memory rewriting the effective system prompt each session), not from an explicit autonomy or runtime-limits artifact.
